title: Add RSS/Atom feed generation for model changelog + subscription docs
author: Wei Chen
description: Summary: This PR adds customer-facing RSS and Atom feeds for the new Model Release Notes (model changelog) section, and documents how customers can subscribe. The feed content is generated at build-time from the published changelog feed (JSON) produced by the control plane, consistent with the docs IA added in #982 and the template/style linting rules in #995. Motivation: Multiple customers have asked for a machine-readable subscription mechanism (RSS/Atom) to support change-management workflows and internal alerting. We also want parity with the docs navigation for release notes so customers can discover the feeds without needing to inspect URLs. Scope: 1) Generate RSS + Atom feeds at /model-release-notes/feed.rss.xml and /model-release-notes/feed.atom.xml. 2) Add per-model feeds at /model-release-notes/{model_id}/feed.rss.xml and /model-release-notes/{model_id}/feed.atom.xml. 3) Add a short docs page (and link from the Model Release Notes landing page) explaining what’s in the feed, how often it updates, and examples for subscribing via browser/Slack/email tools. 4) Ensure feeds only include customer-safe fields (title, summary, published date, model_id/version_id, compatibility notes, deprecation timelines, and canonical links), aligned with the public_changelog_fields allowlist. Implementation details: - Introduces a small generator module in docs build that reads the existing published changelog cache artifact (downloaded during build) and emits two feed formats using a consistent item mapping. - Deterministic ordering: newest first; secondary sort by event_id when multiple entries share the same published timestamp (mirrors generator fix in platform PR for same-day collapse). - Uses stable GUIDs: "model_changelog:{model_id}:{version_id}:{event_id}" so consumers don’t treat edits as new entries. - Handles corrections/supersedes: If an entry is marked as superseded in the published feed, we include it as an item but set the title prefix to "(Superseded)" and ensure the canonical link points to the superseding entry; corrected entries appear normally. - Adds tests for feed validity (well-formed XML, required fields present, max length constraints for summaries) and a snapshot test to prevent accidental schema drift. Docs changes: - New page: "Subscribing to model release notes" under Model Release Notes section. - Adds UI links on the landing page: "RSS" and "Atom" with short helper text. - Adds per-model page link block: "Subscribe to updates for this model". Notes/Non-goals: - This does not add a real-time streaming feed; it updates on docs publish cadence. - We do not include internal fields or raw eval artifacts; we only link to customer-accessible dashboards/evals when present in the published entry. Rollout: Behind the existing "model-release-notes" docs feature flag in staging; in production this will ship with the next docs deploy once the upstream published feed endpoint is enabled. Screenshots: N/A (feed endpoints).

review_conversation: Elliot Price (review): Can we confirm that we’re not emitting any internal-only fields (e.g., internal model nicknames, vendor notes) into the feed? I’d like to see the mapping explicitly restricted to the public allowlist.

Wei Chen (author): Good call. I updated the mapping to only read from the published feed’s customer-safe fields (title/customer_safe_summary/compatibility/deprecation + canonical_url). Added a unit test that fails if unknown fields are referenced.

Kira Thompson (review): Subscription doc is good but please add a section for enterprise change-management: recommended consumption patterns + reminder that feeds update on docs publish cadence (not real-time). Also please avoid implying SLA on publish lag.

Wei Chen (author): Added an "Enterprise workflows" section with guidance (RSS readers, internal ticket automation), and clarified cadence language to "typically daily" and "may be delayed during maintenance" without SLA claims.
Tessa Morgan (review): On the landing page, can we make the RSS/Atom links visually quieter? Also, consider per-model feed discoverability on model pages.
Wei Chen (author): Updated link styling to match other utility links and added a small "Subscribe" block on per-model pages. No design changes beyond existing utility link pattern.

Elliot Price (review): One more thing: GUID stability for corrections. If a published entry is corrected (supersedes), do we keep the old GUID for the original item? Some readers might treat it as a new entry if GUID changes.

Wei Chen (author): We keep GUID tied to (model_id, version_id, event_id). A correction creates a new event_id, so it’s a new item; the previous item is marked "(Superseded)" and links to the corrected one. This matches platform auditability requirements and avoids silent edits.
Elliot Price (approve): Approved. Please ensure we mention that corrected entries appear as a new item to preserve audit history.
Kira Thompson (approve): Approved with the enterprise wording updates.
